WHY IT HAS TO EXIST

Two companies read
the world’s morning mail.

The most personal document stream in your life (contracts, medical letters, password resets, love and grief) flows through infrastructure owned by a handful of firms whose business model is knowing you. Leaving is technically possible and practically punished.

F·01

The concentration is near-total

Gmail alone is estimated at around two billion accounts, and industry measurements attribute roughly three-quarters of all email opens to just Apple’s and Google’s mail clients. Email is a protocol; the inbox became an oligopoly.

F·02

Inside the ad machine

Google stopped scanning Gmail content for ad targeting in 2017, but the inbox still lives inside an advertising company’s ecosystem, feeding an identity that follows you across the company’s other properties. The mail is the moat.

F·03

Independence is punished

Run your own server by the book (SPF, DKIM, DMARC, clean lists) and the big providers may spam-folder you anyway, because your IP has no history with them. The deliverability wall is the lock-in, and it is undocumented by design.

F·04

Privacy mail proved the demand

Proton grew past a hundred million accounts on the promise of mail outside the ad economy. The demand is proven; the missing piece is the full-system offer: the whole stack, owned.

TWO COMPANIES’ MAIL CLIENTS HANDLE ROUGHLY THREE-QUARTERS OF THE WORLD’S EMAIL OPENS

WHAT IT CHANGES

The whole stack,
on metal we hold.

Most “private email” is a client on someone else’s cloud. VF Mail is the full system (transport, storage, shield and interface), with the hard part, deliverability, run as a managed discipline so you never fight that war yourself.

An address that answers to you.

Your mail on infrastructure we hold and you can leave: full export, standard protocols, no hostage data. Ownership means the door opens from the inside.

The reputation war, handled.

Warmed IPs, strict authentication, feedback loops, blocklist vigilance: we run the deliverability battle for you as an operations discipline. That is the product’s hardest promise: an operation we run, with no claim of a magic fix.

A shield on the front door.

Spam and phishing defence at the server, aggressive transport encryption, and none of the engagement machinery: no ads, no tracking pixels of our own, no profile built from your correspondence.

THE MECHANICS

Modern stack,
old-school ownership.

The build stands on the modern self-hosted mail generation (hardened, memory-safe server software on clean-IP metal), wrapped in the operational layer that makes owned mail practical for people with lives. Like every VF system, it leaves the lab with the engine fitted and the harness tuned.

LAYER 1

The transport core

A modern, memory-safe mail server stack (the Stalwart generation of software) on clean-reputation infrastructure in EU jurisdiction, with full standards compliance: SPF, DKIM, DMARC, MTA-STS, DANE.

LAYER 2

The shield layer

Inbound filtering, phishing and malware defence, and outbound reputation protection: the security department a mail admin wishes they had, built into the service.

LAYER 3

The reputation operation

IP warming, deliverability monitoring, blocklist response and provider-relations discipline, run continuously. Owned mail usually fails at this layer, which is why VF Mail ships as an operated system.

LAYER 4

The inbox surface

Clean web and mobile clients plus full IMAP/SMTP for any client you prefer. The interface follows the house style: quiet, fast, and structurally incapable of advertising to you.

QUESTIONS

Asked.
Answered.

Can I download VF Mail today?

Yes. VF Mail is in Early Access and free until November 1. Linux ships as a native AppImage or .deb with a one-line installer that verifies SHA-256 and needs no root. Windows builds from source with one PowerShell command that installs Rust and WebView2 silently, no admin. The notarised macOS .dmg lands with the paid launch on November 1.

What does Early Access include?

The full VF Mail: a sovereign vault, end-to-end encrypted mail between VF users, encrypted direct messages, a real Files system on your own disk, and offline everything. There is no signup, no telemetry and no analytics. When the paid launch flips on November 1, your vault carries forward and you keep a founder-tier discount for life.

Can I use my own domain and my usual mail client?

Yes. Bring your own domain, or use a vfempire.mail alias; a custom domain is included from the first tier. VF Mail speaks IMAP and SMTP everywhere, so any client you prefer works alongside the house web and mobile clients. Migration from Gmail, Fastmail or Proton is a one-click import, and you can leave again with a full export.

What will VF Mail cost after launch?

There is no free tier; a thirty-day trial takes its place. Mailbox is €3.99 a month for one mailbox with 10 GB and a custom domain. Family is €9.99 a month for five mailboxes and 50 GB. Teams is €4.99 per user a month with 25 GB on your company domain. The price you join at is the price you renew at.

Where is my mail stored and who can read it?

On EU metal in Malta, encrypted at rest, under EU jurisdiction. The transport core is a modern, memory-safe server stack of the Stalwart generation with SPF, DKIM, DMARC, MTA-STS and DANE. There are no ads, no tracking pixels of our own and no profile built from your correspondence, and the door opens from the inside: standard protocols, no hostage data.

Will my mail reach Gmail and Outlook inboxes?

Deliverability is the hardest promise in owned mail, and VF Mail runs it as a managed operation: warmed IPs, strict authentication, feedback loops, blocklist vigilance and provider-relations discipline, continuously. The first @vfempire.com inboxes already run on the node, so the playbook is written from real correspondence and real deliverability battles. VF claims no magic fix, only the operation.
